rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An exegetical view identifies the revived person as the Prophet, given Islam, prophethood, and wisdom, and the one in darkness as Abu Jahl in disbelief.
rows.anchor: جاء في التفسير أنه يعني به النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - وأبو جهل بن هشام

words: وَجَعَلْنَا لَهُۥ نُورًا يَمْشِى بِهِۦ فِى ٱلنَّاسِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: More generally, the verse applies to anyone God guides or leaves astray: the guided person is like the dead brought to life and illuminated by wisdom and faith.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن تكون هذه الآية عامة لكل من هداه الله ولكل من أضله الله

words: كَمَن مَّثَلُهُۥ فِى ٱلظُّلُمَٰتِ لَيْسَ بِخَارِجٍ مِّنْهَا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disbeliever is like someone trapped in darkness and unable to escape it.
rows.anchor: ومثل الكافر مثل من هو في الظلمات لا يتخلص منها

words: كَذَٰلِكَ جَعَلْنَا فِى كُلِّ قَرْيَةٍ أَكَٰبِرَ مُجْرِمِيهَا لِيَمْكُرُوا۟ فِيهَا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In 6:123, the kaf is accusative and coordinated with the preceding likewise clause; the sense is that God adorned their deeds in the same way just described.
rows.anchor: موضع الكاف نصب معطوفة على ما قبلها، وهو قوله:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As with that example, God makes the leading criminals in every town plot; their status and wealth more readily draw them into plotting and disbelief.
rows.anchor: لأن الأكابر ما هم فيه من الرياسة والسعة أدعى لهم إلى المكر والكفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their plotting comes back upon them, because they are punished for it.
rows.anchor: أي ذلك المكر يحيق بهم، لأنهم بمكرهم يعذبون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The jinn have greatly increased their number from among the humans they led astray.
rows.anchor: المعنى قد استكثرتم ممن أضللتموهم من الإنس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An exegetical report says humans sought a valley's jinn lord for protection while traveling or hunting; jinn benefited when humans acknowledged their power to protect.
rows.anchor: جاء في التفسير أن استمتاع الإنس بالجن أن الرجل كان إذا سافر سفرا فخاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording points to humans accepting the jinn's misleading enticements; only a few people sought refuge with jinn, so that practice is not the main sense.
rows.anchor: والذي يدل عليه اللفظ - والله أعلم - هو قبول الإنس من الجن ما كانوا يغوونهم به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mathwā means a place of residence or abiding.
rows.anchor: المثوى المقام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khālidīn is accusative as a circumstantial expression: Hell is their abode in a state of enduring residence.
rows.anchor: منصوب على الحال، المعنى: النار مقامكم في حال خلود دائم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception may exclude the period from their rising from the graves through the gathering and their time being reckoned on Judgment Day.
rows.anchor: فقال خالدين فيها مذ يبعثون إلا ما شاء ربك من مقدار حشرهم من قبورهم، ومقدار مدتهم في محاسبتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the exception may refer to kinds of punishment God chooses to add; Zajjaj gives this as another possible reading of the exception.
rows.anchor: وجائز أن يكون إلا ما شاء الله أن يعذبهم به من أصناف العذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is wise in assigning their recompense and wise in all else.
rows.anchor: أي هو حكيم فيما جعله من جزائهم، وحكيم في غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The messengers were humans, but the collective address can say messengers came from both groups because jinn and humans share rationality and are addressed as a rational community.
rows.anchor: لأن الجماعة تعقل وتخاطب، فالرسل: هم بعض من يعقل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase is like saying pearls come from both seas, although they come only from the salt sea, since the two seas have been mentioned together.
rows.anchor: وهذا كقوله: عز وجل: (يخرج منهما اللؤلؤ والمرجان)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The animals meant by every clawed creature are camels and ostriches, since ostriches have claws like camels.
rows.anchor: ئعنى به الإبل والنعام، لأن النعام ذوات ظفر كالإبل

rows.speaker: بعض الناس
rows.claim: One reported view forbids the caul fats and allows the other fats carried on the backs.
rows.anchor: فقال بعض الناس:. حرمت عليهم الثروب، وأحل لهم ما سواها مما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ḥawāyā are the entrails; the singular is given as ḥāwiya, ḥāwiyāʾ, or ḥawiyya.
rows.anchor: وهي المباعر واحدها حاوية وحاوياء وحوية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fat mixed with bone includes tail fat; this is the more common of the two opinions.
rows.anchor: نحو شحم الإلية. وهذا أكثر القولين

words: إِلَّا مَا حَمَلَتْ ظُهُورُهُمَآ أَوِ ٱلْحَوَايَآ أَوْ مَا ٱخْتَلَطَ بِعَظْمٍۢ
rows.speaker: قوم
rows.claim: Another group construes the categories after the caul prohibition as including back-carried fat, entrail fat, or fat mixed with bone, and explicitly says what the backs carry is not forbidden.
rows.anchor: وقال قوم حرمت عليهم الثروب. وأحل لهم ما حملت الظهور وصارت الحوايا أو ما اختلط بعظم

words: أَوِ ٱلْحَوَايَآ أَوْ مَا ٱخْتَلَطَ بِعَظْمٍۢ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here aw marks permissive alternatives: each named person or category can independently be avoided or selected; it need not mean that all are treated only as a joint set.
rows.anchor: دخلت على طريق الإباحة، كما قال جل وعز

words: أَوِ ٱلْحَوَايَآ أَوْ مَا ٱخْتَلَطَ بِعَظْمٍۢ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disjunctive wording is more emphatic than wa: in a prohibition, aw can mean none of the listed parties should be obeyed, while in an instruction to associate, any or all listed people are suitable.
rows.anchor: فليس المعنى أني آمرك بمجالسة واحد منهم، ولكن معنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥītān is the plural of ḥūt; Arabs most commonly call fish ḥītān or nīnān.
rows.anchor: حيتان - جمع حوت، وأكثر ما تسمي العرب السمك الحيتان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first idh is accusative; the sense is to ask them about the time they transgressed on the Sabbath.
rows.anchor: نصب، المعنى سلهم عن عدوهم في السبت، أي سلهم عن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second idh is also accusative, governed by yaʿdūn: ask them when they transgressed at the time the fish came.
rows.anchor: المعنى سلهم إذ عدوا في وقت الإتيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shurraʿan means conspicuously exposed; the fish came openly, so the people trapped them on the Sabbath and took them Sunday.
rows.anchor: أي ظاهرة، وكانت الحيتان تأتي ظاهرة فكانوا يحتالون بحبسها في يوم السبت ثم يأخذونها في يوم الأحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report also says they brazenly took the fish on the Sabbath itself.
rows.anchor: ويقال إنهم جاهروا بأخذها في يوم السبت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The test was made severe because of their wickedness; kāf is accusative with nabluwhum, the preferred analysis.
rows.anchor: أي شددت عليهم المحنة بفسقهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A more remote possibility takes the clause to mean fish did not come visibly when they did not keep Sabbath; nabluwhum then begins a new sentence, but the first analysis is better.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل - على بعد - أن يكون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Limā originally has an alif; Arabic deletes that alif after prepositions, as in famā and ʿam.
rows.anchor: الأصل لما، ولكن الألف تحذف مع حروف الجر نحو لم وعم وبم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The questioners reproached the admonishers because they thought the people would not desist; that was their predominant assessment of the people.
rows.anchor: ومعنى الآية أنهم لاموهم في عظة قوم يعلمون أنهم غير مقلعين. هذا الأغلب عليهم في العلم بهم

words: ٱللَّهُ مُهْلِكُهُمْ أَوْ مُعَذِّبُهُمْ عَذَابًا شَدِيدًا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Given what they saw of the people's deeds, the admonishers said the people would inevitably be destroyed in this world or severely punished in the next.
rows.anchor: أعمالهم - أنهم مهلكون في الدنيا أو معذبون في الآخرة لا محالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They mean that admonishing the people is their excuse before God; commanding right is incumbent on them, and the people might benefit and become mindful.
rows.anchor: قالوا موعظتنا إياهم معذرة إلى ربكم ولعلهم يتقون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Maʿdhiratan may be accusative as a verbal noun, meaning that they apologize with an apology.
rows.anchor: ويجوز النصب في " معذرة " فيكون المعنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nasū can mean they abandoned what they were reminded of, or that their abandonment was like the act of someone who forgot.
rows.anchor: (نسوا) يجوز أن يكون في معنى تركوا، ويجوز أن يكون تركهم بمنزلة من نسي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Baʾīs means severe; the verb baʾisa yabʾusu baʾsan is used when something becomes severe.
rows.anchor: أي شديد، يقال بئس يبؤس بأسا إذا اشتد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reported account divides the people into three groups: those doing evil, those forbidding it, and those who refrained from forbidding it.
rows.anchor: وقيل إن القوم كانوا ثلاث فرق، فرقة عملت بالسوء، وفرقة نهت عن السوء، وفرقة أمسكت عن النهي

words: أَنجَيْنَا ٱلَّذِينَ يَنْهَوْنَ عَنِ ٱلسُّوٓءِ وَأَخَذْنَا ٱلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا۟
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another account has two groups, the forbidders and the evildoers; believers among the forbidders who were displeased with evil were saved with them, while Sabbath transgressors were punished.
rows.anchor: وقيل كانوا فرقتين، فرقة نهت عن السوء وفرقة عملت بالسوء، وبعض الفرقة التي فيها من نهى عن السوء مؤمن

rows.speaker: قوم
rows.claim: One view says the heirs of scripture took bribes for unjust judgments.
rows.anchor: قيل إنهم كانوا يرتشون على الحكم، ويحكمون بجور

rows.speaker: قوم
rows.claim: A second view says they took bribes even when rendering just judgments; either way the gain was paltry.
rows.anchor: وقيل إنهم كانوا يرتشون ويحكمون بحق، وكل ذلك عرض خسيس

words: وَيَقُولُونَ سَيُغْفَرُ لَنَا وَإِن يَأْتِهِمْ عَرَضٌ مِّثْلُهُ يَأْخُذُوهُ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They expected forgiveness without repenting after taking bribes; taking another similar gain shows they persisted, although forgiveness for grave sins is promised with repentance.
rows.anchor: دليل على إصرارهم على الذنب، والله جل وعز وعد بالمغفرة في العظائم

words: أَلَمْ يُؤْخَذْ عَلَيْهِم مِّيثَٰقُ ٱلْكِتَٰبِ أَن لَّا يَقُولُوا۟ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ إِلَّا ٱلْحَقَّ وَدَرَسُوا۟ مَا فِيهِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They knew the covenant of scripture because they had studied what it contained.
rows.anchor: أي فهم ذاكرون لما أخذ عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alladhīna is nominative; the issue is how to link the promise that God does not waste the reformers' reward to those who hold the Book.
rows.anchor: في موضع رفع، وفيها قولان، أعني في (إنا لا نضيع أجر المصلحين)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zajjaj prefers that the promise means the reformers among them: nonbelievers' good deeds are lost, and a reformer is a believer who remains faithful and fulfills duties in belief and practice.
rows.anchor: قال قوم: إنا لا نضيع أجر المصلحين منهم، وهو الذي نختار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Holding the Book means believing it and judging by its contents; the reformer among them stays in faith and performs its obligations in conviction and action.
rows.anchor: أي يؤمنون به، ويحكمون بما فيه إنا لا نضيع أجر المصلح منهم والمصلح المقيم على الإيمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The parallel promise that God does not waste the reward of one who does good likewise means those who do good among the believers.
rows.anchor: أي لا نضيع أجر من أحسن منهم عملا

rows.speaker: قوم
rows.claim: Others say the word reformers changes form from its antecedent while referring to the same people in sense; a semantic antecedent can license the return reference.
rows.anchor: وقال قوم: المصلحون لفظ يخالف لفظ الأول، ومعناه معنى الأول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zajjaj distinguishes a mere name from a semantic equivalent: one cannot say Zayd stood, Abu Amr, but can equate believer with one who fears God and resume it with a pronoun.
rows.anchor: لأن معنى من اتقى الله معنى المؤمن، فقد صار بمنزلة قولك زيد ضربته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ʿafw means surplus or what comes without effort.
rows.anchor: والعفو الفضل، والعفو ما أتى بغير كلفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ʿurf means what is recognized as good, the maʿrūf.
rows.anchor: أي بالمعروف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nazgh is the slightest movement or nudge; of Satan it means a whisper that touches someone.
rows.anchor: قد نزغته إذا حركته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word ṭāʾif is associated with ṭuftu aṭūfu and with a phantom that circles.
rows.anchor: يقال: طفت أطوف، وطاف الخيال يطيف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They reflected on the clearer proof available to them.
rows.anchor: أي تفكروا فيما هو أوضح لهم من الحجة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mubṣirūn means that they see with insight.
rows.anchor: على بصيرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zajjaj says the passage involves fronting and links its sense to the preceding statement that the invoked beings cannot help the people or themselves.
rows.anchor: لا يستطيعون نصركم ولا أنفسهم ينصرون

words: وَإِخْوَٰنُهُمْ يَمُدُّونَهُمْ فِى ٱلْغَىِّ ثُمَّ لَا يُقْصِرُونَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their brothers are the devils, since disbelievers are brothers of devils; al-ghayy is ignorance and falling into action.
rows.anchor: يعني الشياطين، لأن الكفار إخوان الشياطين، والغي الجهل، والوقوع في الحركة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verbs for desisting occur as both aqṣara yaqṣuru and qaṣara yaqṣuru.
rows.anchor: ويقال أقصر يقصر، وقصر، يقصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their challenge means, Why did you not invent an ayah and bring it on your own? The Prophet explained that signs come from God.
rows.anchor: فأعلمهم - صلى الله عليه وسلم - أن الآيات من قبل الله جل ثناؤه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This refers to the Quran brought by the Prophet as insights from God; baṣāʾir is the plural of baṣīra.
rows.anchor: أي هذا القرآن الذي أتيت به بصائر من ربكم، واحدة البصائر بصيرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Baṣāʾir and baṣīra can mean channels or paths of blood.
rows.anchor: والبصيرة والبصائر طرائق الدم، قال الأشعر الجعفي

rows.speaker: الأشعر الجعفي
rows.claim: Al-Ashʿar al-Juʿfi's line uses baṣāʾir and baṣīratī for the blood channels or paths on bodies.
rows.anchor:
قال الأشعر الجعفي.
راحوا بصائرهم على أكتافهم. . .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Baṣīra can also mean a shield, with baṣāʾir as its plural.
rows.anchor: والبصيرة الترس، وجمعها بصائر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Across these usages, the common idea is the appearance and clarity of a thing.
rows.anchor: وجميع هذا أيضا معناه ظهور الشيء وبيانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says conversation in prayer was once allowed, including asking how many units had been prayed; after this verse it was prohibited except for devotional remembrance and requests for pardon.
rows.anchor: يروى أن الكلام في الصلاة كان جائزا، فكان يدخل الرجل فيقول:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reported prohibition exempts speech that draws near to God, such as glorification, profession of divine unity, magnification, and seeking forgiveness.
rows.anchor: التسبيح والتهليل والتكبير والاستغفار وما أشبه ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another possible sense is to act according to the Quran and not go beyond it; hearing God's prayer means that He answers it, since He hears and knows.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون فاستمعوا له وأنصتوا، اعملوا بما فيه ولا تجاوزوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What gives life can mean knowledge, which is a cause of life.
rows.anchor: أي لما يكون سببا للحياة وهو العلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, it can mean what causes lasting life in the bliss of the afterlife.
rows.anchor: وجائز أن يكون لما يكون سببا للحياة الدائمة، في نعيم الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Istajībū has the sense of ajībū, answer or respond.
rows.anchor: ومعنى استجيبوا في معنى أجيبوا

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: The poet's phrase lam yastajibhu means that no one answered the caller, illustrating the synonymy of istajāba and ajāba.
rows.anchor:
قال الشاعر:
وداع دعا يا من يجيب إلى الندا.

words: أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَحُولُ بَيْنَ ٱلْمَرْءِ وَقَلْبِهِۦ
rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: One view says God comes between a believer and disbelief, and between a disbeliever and faith by death, blocking what a person keeps putting off.
rows.anchor: قال بعضهم يحول بين المؤمن والكفر، ويحول بين الكافر والإيمان بالموت

words: أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَحُولُ بَيْنَ ٱلْمَرْءِ وَقَلْبِهِۦ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second view takes the phrase to mean that God is near each person at this degree, like the statement that He is nearer than the jugular vein.
rows.anchor: أن الله مع المرء في القرب بهذه المنزلة

words: أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَحُولُ بَيْنَ ٱلْمَرْءِ وَقَلْبِهِۦ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further explanation is that God can replace believers' fear of the enemy with security, and make their apparently confident enemy weak and fearful.
rows.anchor: فأعلم الله جل ثناؤه أنه يحول بين المرء وقلبه بأن يبدله بالخوف الأمن

words: وَٱتَّقُوا۟ فِتْنَةً لَّا تُصِيبَنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا۟ مِنكُمْ خَآصَّةً
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning concerns a divine punishment falling on the prominent hypocrites who turned people away from belief in God.
rows.anchor: أي اتقوا أن يبدل الظالمون بنقمة من الله، يعنى بهذا مردة المنافقين الذين كانوا يصدون عن الإيمان بالله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some grammarians analyze the clause as a conditional result with the form of a prohibition: dismount, and it will not throw you; the emphatic nūn strengthens it.
rows.anchor: وزعم بعض النحويين أن الكلام جزاء فيه طرف من النهي، فإذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ant commands entry and phrases the warning not to be crushed as a prohibition addressed to Solomon, though its meaning is directed to the ants; similarly, lā arayannaka means do not be here where I see you.
rows.anchor: إنها أمرت بالدخول ثم نهتهم أن يحطمهم سليمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Gabriel and Michael are already included in the general mention of angels but are named separately for their special distinction.
rows.anchor: فذكر جملة الملائكة، فقد دخل جبريل وميكال في الجملة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The named recipients of shares, booty, and charity are highlighted because they are among the most important recipients of charitable funds.
rows.anchor: وكذلك ذكر هؤلاء في القسمة والفيء والصدقة، لأنهم من أهم من يصرف إليه الأموال من البر والصدقة

rows.speaker: أبو إسحاق
rows.claim: Abu Ishaq cites Malik's support from the charity categories in 2:215: one may give to those categories, to only one category, or elsewhere, with no disagreement on that point.
rows.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق: ومن الحجة لمالك أيضا قول الله عز وجل:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In one parse, in kuntum attaches to the preceding 8:40 command to know God is your patron: trust that He aided you, since you witnessed His aid.
rows.anchor: يجوز أن يكون " إن كنتم " معلقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, in kuntum attaches to the command about the spoils: if you believe, accept the rule that a fifth belongs to God and the Messenger, who decide its use.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون (إن كنتم آمنتم بالله) معناها:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Day of Furqān is Badr, where God sent angels to reinforce the Muslims and distinguished truth from falsehood.
rows.anchor: هو يوم بدر، لأن الله عز وجل أظهر فيه من نصره بإرداف الملائكة والإمداد بهم للمسلمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The description of the two camps' locations further clarifies the decisive contrast in God's aid at Badr.
rows.anchor: فقال عز وجل: (إذ أنتم بالعدوة الدنيا وهم بالعدوة القصوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-dunyā is the nearer side; al-ʿidwa is a valley bank, with the banks located toward Medina and Mecca.
rows.anchor: أي الدنيا منكم، والعدوة شفير الوادي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The farther bank was the edge of the valley on the Mecca side.
rows.anchor: بشفير الوادي الذي يلي مكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-rakb is the caravan led by Abu Sufyan, which was on the seashore.
rows.anchor: الركب: العير التي كان فيها أبو سفيان على شاطئ البحر

words: وَلَٰكِن لِّيَقْضِىَ ٱللَّهُ أَمْرًا كَانَ مَفْعُولًا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muslims faced sinking sand and no water, while the better-positioned polytheists had water and guarded the caravan; victory despite their smaller numbers and weaker position made God's aid a decisive distinction.
rows.anchor: وكان المشركون نازلين على موضع فيه الماء، وهم مع ذلك يحامون عن العير، فهو أشد لشوكتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The recited accusative makes the caravan a place lower than you; a permissible nominative instead predicates that the caravan is lower or farther down.
rows.anchor: الوجه أن تنصب (أسفل)، وعليه القراءة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God makes the seeker of truth like a living person and the misguided like one who has perished.
rows.anchor: جعل الله عز وجل القاصد للحق بمنزلة الحي، وجعل الضال بمنزلة الهالك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Both ḥayiya with two explicit yāʾs and ḥayya with an assimilated doubled yāʾ are reported readings.
rows.anchor: ويجوز حيي بياءين، وحي بياء مشددة مدغمة، وقد قرئ بهما جميعا

rows.speaker: الخليل وسيبويه
rows.claim: Al-Khalil and Sibawayh permit either assimilation or clear pronunciation when the second vowel is fixed; assimilation joins like letters, while clear pronunciation reflects the changed form of the second yāʾ.
rows.anchor: فأما الخليل وسيبويه فيجيزان الإدغام والإظهار إذا كانت الحركة في الثاني لازمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Clear pronunciation is supported by the forms ḥayiya yaḥyā, al-maḥyā, and al-mamāt.
rows.anchor: وأما من أظهر فلأن الحرف الثاني ينتقل عن لفظ الياء، تقول حيي يحيا، والمحيا والممات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For yuhyī and the verse about reviving the dead, Basran grammarians unanimously require two clear yāʾs; some others allow a single assimilated yāʾ.
rows.anchor: فلا يجوز فيه عند جميع البصريين إلا يحيي بياءين ظاهرتين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zajjaj rejects an anonymous anomalous poem as evidence for assimilation, since its poet and tribe are unknown and the Quran must not rest on an unidentified recitation or a stray verse.
rows.anchor: وليس ينبغي أن يحمل كتاب الله على " أنشدني بعضهم " ولا على بيت شاذ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even for non-weak consonants such as in lam yawad, clear gemination is preferred when the second letter would be still; a weak final letter gives no stronger case for assimilation.
rows.anchor: نحو: " لم يود " فالاختيار إظهار التضعيف

rows.speaker: النحويون
rows.claim: Grammarians prefer yawm yaʾtī with a written yāʾ, while the codex and reciters have yaʾt with a kasra and no yāʾ.
rows.anchor: الذي يختاره النحويون: يوم يأتي لا تكلم نفس إلا بإذنه.

rows.speaker: الخليل وسيبويه
rows.claim: The Hudhayl dialect often deletes final yāʾs; Khalil and Sibawayh note forms such as lā adri, where frequent use permits deletion with kasra remaining.
rows.anchor: وهذيل تستعمل حذف هذه الياءات كثيرا. وقد ذكر سيبويه والخليل أن العرب تقول لا أدر فتحذف الياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although writing the yāʾ is grammatically better, Zajjaj prefers the codex reading followed by all reciters, since recitation is transmitted practice and has an Arabic parallel.
rows.anchor: والأجود في النحو إثبات الياء والذي أراه اتباع المصحف مع إجماع القراء، لأن القراءة سنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent conflict with other verses saying people do not speak or are questioned is resolved by distinguishing kinds of speech and different scenes of Judgment Day.
rows.anchor: وهذه الآية فيها سؤال أكثر ما يسأل عنه أهل الإلحاد في الدين

rows.speaker: العلماء المتقدمون
rows.claim: Early Muslim language scholars explain the question as rebuke and confirmation, establishing proof against people whose deeds God already knows.
rows.anchor: فسألهم سؤال توبيخ وتقرير لإيجاب الحجة عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No one is asked about sin in order to discover it; God knew their deeds before they performed them.
rows.anchor: أي لا يسأل ليعلم ذلك منه، لأن الله قد علم أعمالهم قبل أن يعملوها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They do speak to confess sins, blame one another, and shift blame, but do not speak an argument that benefits them; thus they can be said not to speak.
rows.anchor: أي لا ينطقون بحجة تجب لهم، وإنما يتكلمون بالإقرار بذنوبهم ولوم بعضهم بعضا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling those without a valid argument silent resembles telling a talkative person with empty speech that he has not spoken; disbelievers are likewise deaf and blind because they do not accept or reflect.
rows.anchor: للذي يخاطبك كثيرا وخطابه فارغ من الحجة: ما تكلمت بشيء

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: The poet says a person can be deaf to what displeases him while still hearing, illustrating figurative deafness.
rows.anchor:
قال الشاعر:
أصم عما ساءه سميع

rows.speaker: قوم
rows.claim: Another view says Judgment Day is long, with stations where speech is forbidden and others where it is permitted; Zajjaj considers both explanations sound.
rows.anchor: وقال قوم: ذلك اليوم طويل وله مواضع ومواطن ومواقف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zafīr is a severe, ugly groan.
rows.anchor: من شديد الأنين وقبيحه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shahīq is a very severe, high-pitched groan.
rows.anchor: والشهيق الأنين الشديد المرتفع جدا

rows.speaker: أهل اللغة من البصريين والكوفيين
rows.claim: Basran and Kufan linguists compare zafīr to the beginning of a donkey's bray and shahīq to its ending.
rows.anchor: وزعم أهل اللغة من البصريين والكوفيين أن الزفير بمنزلة ابتداء صوت الحمار في النهيق، والشهيق بمنزلة آخر صوته

rows.speaker: أهل اللغة البصريين والكوفيين
rows.claim: One joint Basran and Kufan account takes illā as siwā, 'apart from': the stated span of abiding is qualified by what God wills to be omitted or added.
rows.anchor:
قولان منها لأهل اللغة البصريين والكوفيين جميعا.
قالوا: المعنى خالدين فيها إلا ما شاء ربك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Basran and Kufan grammarians' second account treats the phrase as saying 'unless I will otherwise': God could remove them, but has informed us that they abide forever.
rows.anchor: وقالوا قولا آخر: (إلا ما شاء ربك) ولا يشاء أن يخرجهم منها

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Another view excludes the interval after resurrection while they stand for the reckoning, then resumes the description of abiding in Hell.
rows.anchor: قال بعضهم إذا حشروا وبعثوا فهم في شروط القيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A fourth view applies the exception to the mentioned groaning: they have it except for other kinds of punishment; likewise Paradise includes delights both mentioned and unmentioned, which Zajjaj says the unbroken gift supports.
rows.anchor: وفيها قول رابع: أن الاستثناء وقع على أن لهم فيها زفيرا وشهيقا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ghayra majdhūdh means not cut off, uninterrupted.
rows.anchor: أي غير مقطوع

rows.speaker: النابعة
rows.claim: Al-Nābigha's lines describe swords cutting through armor, illustrating cutting and severance in Arabic usage.
rows.anchor:
قال النابعة
تقد السلوقي المضاعف نسجه. . . وتوقد بالصفاح نار الحباحب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their allotted share is whatever reaches them, whether good or evil.
rows.anchor: أي نوفيهم ما يصيبهم من خير أو شر
